By Rick Gogreve ,
1 hours ago NEW ORLEANS ( WGNO ) ‚Äî¬†Last year, New Orleans gave the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals a budget of $3.2 million, but now it‚Äôs been cut down to around $2 million. The shelter has had to leave several positions vacant.
‚ÄúOpen positions have been frozen or delayed, so we are not operating at full staff right now. We were very fortunate to not do any layoffs at this point, but again, positions have been frozen. Our service hours have changed, and that‚Äôs based on the need,‚Äù Interim Advancement Director Rebecca Chalin Nguyen said.
The SPCA is no longer doing stray pickup, but their core services have not changed.
‚ÄúThat essential veterinary care we‚Äôre still providing and we‚Äôre still responding to cruelty cases. We are still doing welfare checks. We are still doing those core services,‚Äù Nguyen said.

‚ÄúOur money that we give them for their specific CEA purposes is separate from their actual budget itself,‚Äù Morrell said.
The $2 million funded by the city this year represents just a portion of the full budget.
According to the SPCA, much of the other funds, such as donations, are already allocated for other uses.
‚ÄúWe have funding for different programs. Some of our programs actually generate revenue. Some of them are funded by the city, and when it comes to different sources of income, we‚Äôre just not in a position to subsidize city services,‚Äù Nguyen said.
Now, they‚Äôre looking for any help they can get until their budget returns to normal.
‚ÄúVolunteering, fostering donation, making a donation, any way that you can get involved and help be part of the solution,‚Äù Nguyen said.
